page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores running at 2.7 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the instance mostly in the average tier for general compute tasks. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng benchmarks register at 1890.78 and 7769.13 respectively, while the Passmark CPU score is 11393.05. However, there are notable performance bottlenecks. While cached small-block memory read bandwidth is high at 423.1 GB/sec, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth drops to a weak 33.45 GB/sec. Additionally, Redis SET operations perform in the bottom 25% at 7.96 million operations per second, and medium-model 7B LLM inference prompt processing falls into the poor category at 16.12 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r7t.2xlarge offers a high memory density per vCPU, making it suitable for memory-bound applications that do not require high-speed local storage or intensive GPU acceleration. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and average multi-core performance, this instance is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers with moderate write demands, enterprise applications, and general-purpose memory-intensive workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon 8369B processor at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor, it provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard CPU and compression tasks, though it exhibits weaker performance in uncached large-block memory reads, Redis SET operations, and medium-model LLM inference. Qualitatively, the instance offers balanced resource density for memory-intensive workloads. It is best suited for databases, memory caching, and enterprise applications that require dedicated compute resources without local storage dependencies.
